svg.title: The Select dials, in the order worth turning them, and the two metrics to wire first
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure in two columns. The left column lists seven dials in priority order: the re-ranker on or off, which is the single largest quality lever; k, the packed count, defaulting to five; the top-N candidate set, defaulting to fifty; hybrid weighting, where reciprocal rank fusion works untuned; chunk size, four to six hundred tokens for prose and two to three hundred for code; the embedding model, switched only with an offline benchmark; and query rewriting or HyDE for jargon-heavy corpora. A dashed line after the third marks where the gains flatten. The right column holds the two metrics to wire up first: recall at N offline, the most predictive single number, and citation accuracy online, which catches packing and re-ranking bugs that recall misses.
svg.text: Turn the dials in this order
A team that switches the embedding model before turning on re-ranking is rearranging deck chairs.
the first three move the number
Re-ranker on or off
The single largest quality lever. Always on in production.
k, the packed count
Default 5. Down to 3 for terse, up to 10 for synthesis.
Top-N candidate set
Default 50. Up to 100 for long-tail recall, down to 20 for latency.
Hybrid weighting
RRF works untuned; weighted fusion needs offline labels.
Chunk size
400–600 tokens for prose, 200–300 for code, 10–20% overlap.
Embedding model
Switch only with an offline benchmark behind you.
Query rewriting / HyDE
On for jargon-heavy corpora, optional otherwise.
Wire these up first
Recall@N
offline
Out of a curated query set, what fraction
have the gold passage anywhere in the
top-N? Cheap, and the single most
predictive number for end-to-end quality.
Citation accuracy
online
Does the chunk the model cited actually
contain the fact it asserted? Sample 50
production answers a week and label them.
Catches packing and re-rank bugs recall
misses entirely.
The mistake to avoid is tuning these in the wrong order.
End-to-end answer correctness on a held-out set closes the loop, and is Post 20.
